newsitem.title: CHINA: China religious figures blast U.S. report.
newsitem.headline: China religious figures blast U.S. report.

text.p: Top figures in China's officially recognised religious movements accused the United States of blasphemy on Wednesday, saying a critical U.S. report on freedom of worship in this country was distorted.

China's constitution guaranteed its citizens full freedom of religious belief and protected religious activities, the Xinhua news agency quoted Shi Zesheng, vice-chairman of the Three-Self Patriotic Movement of Protestant Churches in China, as saying.

"The U.S. report totally distorts the actual religious situation in China," Xinhua quoted Min Zhiting, president of the China Taoist Association, as telling a forum of religious leaders and scholars in Beijing.

In a report on freedom of religion around the world, the U.S. State Department last month accused China of violating constitutional pledges on freedom of worship by clamping all religious activity under government control.
Beijing last month slammed the report, accusing the United States of ignorance about religion in China and of trying to meddle in its affairs.

At Wednesday's forum, scholars and representatives of China's main religions of Buddhism, Taoism, Islam, Catholicism and Protestantism dismissed accusations that Beijing had punished religious believers.

"The Chinese Communist Party has been unswervingly pursuing the policy on religious freedom and respecting both religions and religious believers," it quoted Wu Yungui, director of the Religious Research Institute under the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, as saying.
China had not arrested or jailed a single person for their religious beliefs but had punished people who used the cloak of religion to swindle people or engage in criminal activity, Wu as saying.

"Some people flaunt the banner of religion and disrupt public security by resorting to demagogy to engage in seducing female followers," Xinhua quoted Shi of the Three-Self Patriotic Movement as saying.
"People in the U.S. report cited as being involved in so-called 'religious persecution' cases were, in fact, criminals and punishment of criminals has nothing to do with religious belief," Wu said.
The drafters of the U.S. report had "deliberately confused right from wrong and represented nothing more than blasphemy of sacred religious belief," Shi said.

Religion has seen a revival in China in recent years as Beijing has relaxed controls over worship, once suppressed as subversive, and officials say the number of religious faithful has reached 100 million.
However, Beijing's communist rulers still keep a close eye on religious activities, insisting that believers practise their faith through officially controlled or sponsored religious organisations.
Official estimates put the number of Protestants in China at about 10 million but another 20 million are thought to practise their faith in secret through underground churches.
The Beijing-sponsored Chinese Catholic Church claims several million members, while many more have pledged secret allegiance to Rome.
